nl: Write a function `sum_to_n` that takes an index `n` and returns the i32 sum of all indices from 0 up to but excluding `n`, using scf.for with an iter_args accumulator.
Write a function `sum64` that takes an index `n` and returns the i64 sum 0 + 1 + ... + (n-1) computed with an scf.for loop carrying an i64 accumulator.
Write a function `fact` that takes an index `n` and returns n! as an i32, multiplying the loop index plus one into an iter_args accumulator initialized to 1.
Write a function `ipow` that takes an i64 base `b` and an index exponent `n` and returns b raised to the n-th power, using an scf.for loop with an i64 iter_args product starting at 1.
Write a function `sum_range` that takes two index values `lb` and `ub` and returns the i32 sum of every index from `lb` up to but excluding `ub`, using scf.for.
Write a function `sum_even` that takes an index `n` and returns the i32 sum of the indices 0, 2, 4, ... below `n`, using an scf.for loop with step 2.
Write a function `sum_sq` that takes an index `n` and returns the i32 sum of i*i for i from 0 to n-1, using scf.for with an iter_args accumulator.
Write a function `scale` that takes an f32 `x` and an index `n` and returns x added n times to an f32 accumulator starting at 0.0, using scf.for with iter_args.
Write a function `fpow` that takes an f32 `x` and an index `n` and returns x to the n-th power as an f32, multiplying into an iter_args accumulator initialized to 1.0.
Write a function `fsum` that takes an index `n` and returns the f64 sum of the indices 0 .. n-1, converting each index to i64 and then to f64 inside an scf.for loop with an f64 accumulator.
Write a function `tri` that takes an index `n` and returns the triangular number 0 + 1 + ... + (n-1) as an index, using an scf.for loop whose iter_args accumulator has type index.
Write a function `xor_fold` that takes an index `n` and returns the i32 xor of all indices 0 .. n-1, folding with arith.xori into an scf.for iter_args accumulator.
Write a function `imax` that takes two i32 values `a` and `b` and returns the larger one, selecting with an scf.if that yields a result in both branches.
Write a function `fabs` that takes an f32 `x` and returns its absolute value: an scf.if on x < 0.0 yields 0.0 - x in the then branch and x in the else branch.
Write a function `clamp_hi` that takes an f32 `x` and an f32 `hi` and returns hi if x is greater than hi, otherwise x, using scf.if with an f32 result.
Write a function `dh` that takes an f32 `x` and an i1 flag `f` and returns 2x when the flag is true and x/2 otherwise, computing each value inside the corresponding scf.if branch.
Write a function `sign` that takes an i32 `x` and returns 1 if x is greater than 0 and -1 otherwise, using scf.if with an i32 result.
Write a function `addsub` that takes i32 values `a` and `b` and an i1 `s` and returns a + b when s is true, otherwise a - b, with the arithmetic inside the scf.if branches.
Write a function `pick` that takes two index values `a` and `b` and an i1 `c` and returns a if c is true, else b, using scf.if with an index result.

Write a function `minmax_sum` that takes two i32 values `a` and `b` and returns their sum computed as min + max: an scf.if on a < b yields the pair (a, b) or (b, a) as two i32 results, which are then added.

Write a function `clamp` that takes an i32 `x`, a lower bound `lo` and an upper bound `hi` and returns x clamped into [lo, hi]: an outer scf.if handles x < lo, and its else branch contains a second scf.if handling x > hi.

Write a function `pairs` that takes two index values `n` and `m` and returns n * m as an i32 by counting one per iteration of an inner scf.for over m nested inside an outer scf.for over n, threading an i32 accumulator through both loops with iter_args.
Write a function `sum_ij` that takes two index values `n` and `m` and returns the i32 sum of (i + j) over all i in [0, n) and j in [0, m), using two nested scf.for loops with iter_args.
Write a function `sum_prod` that takes two index values `n` and `m` and returns the i64 sum of i * j over all i < n and j < m, computed with nested scf.for loops carrying an i64 accumulator.
Write a function `tri_count` that takes an index `n` and returns the number of pairs (i, j) with j < i < n as an i32, using an outer scf.for over i and an inner scf.for from 0 to i.

Write a function `sum2d` that takes a 2-D f32 memref `a` with dynamic shape and returns the f32 sum of all its elements, using nested scf.for loops over the two memref.dim bounds with an f32 iter_args accumulator.
Write a function `fill2d` that takes a 2-D i32 memref `a` with dynamic shape and an i32 `v` and stores v into every element using nested scf.for loops bounded by memref.dim.
Write a function `scale2d` that takes a 2-D f32 memref `a` with dynamic shape and an f32 `s` and multiplies every element in place by s, using nested scf.for loops over memref.dim bounds.

Write a function `row_sums` that takes a 2-D f32 memref `a` and a 1-D f32 memref `out`, both with dynamic shapes, and stores the sum of each row of a into out: an outer scf.for over rows, an inner scf.for with an f32 iter_args accumulator over columns, then a memref.store.
Write a function `vsum` that takes a 1-D f32 memref `a` with dynamic shape and returns the f32 sum of its elements, looping with scf.for from 0 to memref.dim and accumulating with iter_args.
Write a function `isum` that takes a 1-D i32 memref `a` with dynamic shape and returns the i32 sum of its elements using scf.for with an iter_args accumulator and memref.dim as the bound.
Write a function `iprod` that takes a 1-D i64 memref `a` with dynamic shape and returns the i64 product of its elements, multiplying into an iter_args accumulator initialized to 1.
Write a function `dot` that takes two 1-D f32 memrefs `a` and `b` with dynamic shape and returns their dot product as an f32, using a single scf.for over memref.dim of a with an f32 accumulator.

Write a function `vmax` that takes a 1-D f32 memref `a` with dynamic shape and an f32 `init` and returns the maximum of init and all elements of a, using scf.for with an iter_args accumulator and arith.maximumf.
Write a function `vfill` that takes a 1-D f32 memref `a` with dynamic shape and an f32 `v` and stores v into every element using an scf.for loop over memref.dim.
Write a function `iota` that takes a 1-D i32 memref `a` with dynamic shape and stores the index of each element (cast to i32) into it, using scf.for with arith.index_cast and memref.store.
Write a function `vscale` that takes a 1-D f32 memref `a` with dynamic shape and an f32 `s` and multiplies each element in place by s using scf.for with memref.load and memref.store.

Write a function `axpy` that takes an f32 `alpha` and two 1-D f32 memrefs `x` and `y` with dynamic shape and updates y[i] = alpha * x[i] + y[i] for every i with an scf.for loop bounded by memref.dim of x.
Write a function `vadd` that takes three 1-D f32 memrefs `a`, `b` and `c` with dynamic shape and stores a[i] + b[i] into c[i] for every i using scf.for bounded by memref.dim of a.

Write a function `prefix` that takes a 1-D i32 memref `a` with dynamic shape and replaces each element with the running sum of all elements up to and including it, carrying the running sum as an i32 iter_args value through an scf.for loop.
Write a function `sum_k` that takes a 1-D i32 memref `a` and an index `k` and returns the i32 sum of the first k elements of a, using scf.for from 0 to k with an iter_args accumulator.
Write a function `dsum` that takes a 1-D f64 memref `a` with dynamic shape and returns the f64 sum of its elements with an scf.for loop and an f64 iter_args accumulator.
Write a function `store_if` that takes a 1-D i32 memref `a`, an index `i`, an i32 `v` and an i1 `flag` and stores v into a[i] only when flag is true, using scf.if without results.

Write a function `store_sel` that takes a 1-D f32 memref `a`, an index `i`, two f32 values `x` and `y` and an i1 `c` and stores x into a[i] when c is true and y otherwise, using scf.if with an else region and no results.

Write a function `relu` that takes a 1-D f32 memref `a` with dynamic shape and replaces every negative element with 0.0: an scf.for over memref.dim whose body loads the element and uses a result-less scf.if to store 0.0 when it is less than 0.0.

Write a function `cap` that takes a 1-D i32 memref `a` with dynamic shape and an i32 `t` and replaces every element greater than t with t, using scf.for over memref.dim and a result-less scf.if with a memref.store.

Write a function `double_even` that takes a 1-D i32 memref `a` with dynamic shape and doubles every element whose index is even, using scf.for, arith.remui on the index, and a result-less scf.if around the store.

Write a function `order2` that takes a 1-D f32 memref `a` and two indices `i` and `j`, loads a[i] and a[j], and if a[i] is greater than a[j] swaps them in place using a result-less scf.if with two memref.store ops.

Write a function `mixed` that takes an index `n` and returns, as an f32, the sum of indices 0..n-1 computed twice: once as an i32 and once as an f32, both carried as iter_args of a single scf.for, then converted and added together.

Write a function `mean` that takes a 1-D f32 memref `a` with dynamic shape and returns its mean as an f32: an scf.for carries an i32 element count and an f32 running sum as two iter_args, and the sum is divided by the count converted to f32.

Write a function `ps` that takes an f32 `x` and an index `n` and returns x^n + n as an f32: one f32 iter_args value multiplies x each iteration, an i32 iter_args value counts iterations, and the count is converted to f32 and added at the end.

Write a function `sum_max` that takes a 1-D i32 memref `a` with dynamic shape and an f32 `init` and returns, as an f32, the i32 element sum converted to f32 plus the maximum of init and every element converted to f32, using an scf.for with an i32 and an f32 iter_args.

Write a function `alt` that takes an index `n` and returns the f32 alternating sum 0 - 1 + 2 - 3 ... over indices below n: an scf.for carries an i1 sign flag and an f32 accumulator as iter_args, flipping the flag with arith.xori each iteration.

Write a function `count_pos` that takes a 1-D i32 memref `a` with dynamic shape and returns the i32 number of elements greater than zero: an scf.for with an i32 iter_args accumulator whose body uses an scf.if with an i32 result to add 1 or 0.

Write a function `sum_above` that takes a 1-D f32 memref `a` with dynamic shape and an f32 threshold `t` and returns the f32 sum of the elements greater than t, using an scf.for with an iter_args accumulator and an scf.if with an f32 result inside the loop.

Write a function `fill_if` that takes a 1-D f32 memref `a` with dynamic shape, an f32 `v` and an i1 `go` and, only when go is true, fills every element of a with v using an scf.for loop nested inside a result-less scf.if.

Write a function `sum_or_zero` that takes a 1-D i32 memref `a` with dynamic shape and an i1 `go` and returns the i32 sum of a when go is true and 0 otherwise: an scf.if with an i32 result whose then branch runs an scf.for with an iter_args accumulator.

Write a function `argmax` that takes a 1-D f32 memref `a` with dynamic shape and returns the index of its largest element: an scf.for carries the best value (f32) and best index as two iter_args, updating both through an scf.if with two results when the current element is greater.

Write a function `clamp_store` that takes two 1-D i32 memrefs `src` and `dst` with dynamic shape and an i32 `hi`, and stores min(src[i], hi) into dst[i] for every i, using scf.for and an scf.if with an i32 result to choose the value.

Write a function `vmin` that takes a 1-D i32 memref `a` with dynamic shape and an i32 `init` and returns the minimum of init and every element, using scf.for with an iter_args accumulator and an scf.if with an i32 result instead of arith.minsi.
